cohort: The study included 125 pregnant women beyond 28 weeks of gestation, presenting with pruritus and diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.
finding: Higher serum bile acid levels and severe Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) were positively correlated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including increased rates of induced labor, longer hospital stays, low birth weight, lower APGAR scores, fetal distress, and neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Higher bile acid levels were significantly associated with increased rates of induced labor.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was measured as an outcome.
gest_age: Participants were pregnant women beyond 28 weeks of gestation; gestational age at delivery and preterm birth were measured as outcomes.
